questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How children learn to read at school
Why people today read far fewer books than before
The history of International Literacy Day
Projects that help adults learn to read and write
questions.why: Phil says they'll hear about projects in two countries getting more adults reading and writing.

questions.q: What point does Phil make about reading?
options: It is mainly a hobby for people who commute
It is less important now that almost everyone has a phone
It is needed for everyday tasks like reading labels
It is only useful for reading the news
questions.why: He calls it an essential skill for everyday activities like reading labels when buying groceries.

questions.q: What did the UN report estimate?
options: Over 700 million adults can't read or write
One in six children around the world never goes to school
About 11,000 adults are illiterate
Most illiterate adults live in England
questions.why: Beth says the report estimated that over 700 million adults are illiterate.

questions.q: Why is it hard for children in coastal Bangladesh to get an education?
options: Schools there are very expensive
Regular floods mean families keep moving
There are no teachers in those towns
Children have to work in factories instead of studying
questions.why: Because the towns flood regularly, families are always on the move.

questions.q: How did Rashida sign documents before the Friendship Project?
options: Her children signed for her
She used her fingerprint
She drew a small picture
She never signed anything
questions.why: She says she had to use her fingerprint as a signature.

questions.q: Why does Rashida say “No one can cheat me anymore”?
options: Because she now has a job in a bank
Because her children now look after all of her money
Because she no longer buys anything
Because she can now keep track of her spending
questions.why: She can now read, write and keep an account of her expenses.

questions.q: What do we learn about the Friendship Project?
options: It is free and over 11,000 adults have completed it
It costs a lot but is very successful
It only teaches maths to men
It matches adult learners with trained volunteers in England
questions.why: Phil says the project is free and over 11,000 adults have completed it.

questions.q: How did Peter feel about himself before joining Readeasy?
options: Angry with his old teachers
Proud that he had managed his whole life without reading
Sure he was stupid and would never learn
Happy because his wife read for him
questions.why: After trying college twice, he says, “I'm thick, I'm stupid… it's never gonna work for me.”
